name: ISO 27001
description: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A — Information security controls (technical subset)

controls.name: Authentication information
controls.desc: Authentication secrets must be created, distributed and stored securely. Modern password hashing and root-only shadow file permissions are baseline requirements.

controls.name: Privileged access rights
controls.desc: Privileged access must be restricted and monitored. Extra UID 0 accounts and privileged containers bypass access controls.

controls.name: Secure authentication
controls.desc: Authentication mechanisms must be strong enough to prevent unauthorized access. Password-only SSH and direct root login are insufficient.

controls.name: Technical vulnerability management
controls.desc: Known vulnerabilities must be identified and remediated. This includes patching, strong TLS, and valid certificates.

controls.name: Configuration management
controls.desc: System configurations must be hardened and monitored. World-writable files and excessive SUID binaries indicate weak configuration control.

controls.name: Logging
controls.desc: Security events must be logged and monitored. Excessive failed logins indicate an active attack or misconfiguration.

controls.name: Monitoring activities
controls.desc: Security-relevant kernel events, authentication attempts and time-sync state must be continuously monitored to support detection and forensics.

controls.name: Network security
controls.desc: Networks must be segmented and protected. Active firewalls, disabled IP forwarding, and reverse path filtering are baseline controls.

controls.name: Segregation of networks and container isolation
controls.desc: Network and execution domains must be segregated. Docker containers running with `--privileged` or with a world-accessible socket break out of these isolation boundaries.

controls.name: Use of cryptography
controls.desc: Cryptographic controls must use current standards. Weak protocols and ciphers must be disabled and data at rest encrypted.
